title: [Feature Request] User-configurable auto-compaction threshold in the desktop app (~256K hardcoded while the model window is 1M)

labels.name: others
labels.description: Issues not falling in bug, performance, support, build and install or feature

body:
### Summary

The desktop app auto-compacts once a session reaches roughly 256K tokens (input + cache read), regardless of the model's actual context capacity. For models whose published input limit is 1,048,576 tokens (e.g., Gemini 3.8 Flash), compaction discards verbatim context while more than 75% of the model's native window is still free. There is no user-facing control over the threshold and no warning before it fires.

### Evidence

- Closely related CLI-side request (headless orchestrator focus): #1316 (still open).
- Third-party instrumentation tools confirm the host-reported session window (~256K on app 2.28.2) and that the same host counters decide when compaction is applied. See the public field docs:
  - https://github.com/n2ns/antigravity-panel/blob/main/docs/FEATURES.md ("The values are the Language Server's own estimate, the same figure that decides when the IDE compresses... it lets the context fill up to the limit, then compresses it")
  - https://github.com/YOU-SHOULD-KNOW-ME/antigrative-dashboard/blob/main/docs/CONTEXT_LIMITS.md (denominator = host active window; the author explicitly refuses to substitute the provider's catalog value)
- Gemini 3.8 Flash published input limit: 1,048,576 tokens - https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.8-flash

### Problems in practice

- Long engineering tasks must be split into several conversations with manual handoff of conclusions.
- Compaction discards detailed earlier context; tool outputs and decisions need to be re-derived afterwards.
- Users cannot opt in to using more of the native window even when explicitly accepting higher latency/cost.

### Feature request

1. A user-configurable auto-compaction threshold (per session or per model), as a fraction of the window or absolute tokens - desktop-parity for the knobs requested in #1316.
2. An opt-out ("no auto compact" / "compact only on demand") for workflows that intentionally leverage the provider's native window.
3. A visible warning before compaction happens, so important verbatim context can be exported into a checkpoint/handoff note first.
4. Documentation of the current threshold and whether it varies by model or plan.

If the smaller default is a deliberate product decision, it would still help to let users choose between "platform default" and "provider native window (up to the published limit)".

### Environment

Antigravity desktop app 2.28.2, Windows 10 x64.
